Subject: Hosted API SLOs — initial request and requirements

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. Greenline is evaluating Redwood Hosted to power near-real-time insights for our dashboard product. Before we move toward procurement we need a clear operational commitment for request latency and how you measure it. Attached is a short doc with our desired targets and edge cases (greenline_slo_request.pdf). Summary:

- Target p50 and p95 for the hosted API (US region) for typical inference calls (200–512 tokens).
- Measurement aggregation & windows — we need contractual language around how you compute percentiles (per minute vs rolling windows vs hourly aggregation).
- Transient carveouts we expect you to exclude: orchestrated deployments, cache warmups, and short regional network issues.
- Burst behavior — during predictable daily traffic spikes we need either a temporary capacity guarantee or documented carveout rules.

Our initial target numbers we would find acceptable (negotiable): p50 <= 75ms, p95 <= 300ms. If you can commit to those with documented measurement rules and a clear credit policy we can proceed to contract drafting.

Timeline: we’d like a first-pass SLO operational proposal by EOD Wed (Jan 14) and contract language by Jan 25.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Best,

Greenline Analytics

- Typical carveouts: orchestrated rollout windows, KV-cache priming (first N minutes after model swap), and major region-level network incidents.

Subject: Proposed operational SLOs and measurement details

Hi Ari / Legal — adding the operational detail Marissa promised. Below is a concise proposal intended for contracting discussion. Please review and flag anything that would block procurement.

Operational SLO proposal (hosted, US region) — draft:
- Measurement unit: per-request end-to-end server-side latency for successful inference responses (status code 2xx), measured at the API edge before any client network egress.
- Percentiles: p50 and p95 computed per 1-minute window (all successful requests in that minute), then aggregated into a rolling hourly summary for contractual breach detection.
- Baseline commitment: p50 <= 65ms, p95 <= 295ms for Greenline's expected committed throughput tier (up to 600 qps sustained).
- Carveouts: automated orchestrated rollouts and explicit model swaps (we exclude requests in the first 5 minutes after a model version change in the affected pool), KV-cache priming for the first 3 minutes after cold start, and region-level major network incidents (as declared by Redwood Ops).
- Burst allowance: one 3-minute burst carveout per 24-hour period up to a configurable burst capacity threshold, intended to accommodate predictable traffic spikes. Use beyond that requires pre-notification or it will count against SLOs.
- Sampling and failed requests: failed requests (5xx) are excluded from latency percentile computation but are counted for availability/e2e error SLOs separately.
- Credits: SLA credits scale by the magnitude and duration of p95 breaches against the contractual hourly aggregation. Example: small deviation (p95 exceedance <= 0.5% of measured hour) -> 0.5% credit; larger or repeated breaches scale up — we will provide a formal credit table for contract.

If Greenline Legal prefers a different aggregation window (15-min rolling windows instead of hourly) we can negotiate; however, we recommend hourly contractual aggregation to smooth transient variance while keeping customer-visible dashboards at a higher granularity.

Please let us know any changes; once agreed we'll fold these into a contract addendum and a one-page operational runbook.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

(Attachment: operational_slo_notes.txt — short bullets)

From: Greenline Analytics Legal <legal@greenline.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed operational SLOs and measurement details — legal redlines

Marissa / Karthik — thanks for the draft. Greenline Legal reviewed and has a few requested changes before we sign off:

Quoted for context:
> - Percentiles: p50 and p95 computed per 1-minute window (all successful requests in that minute), then aggregated into a rolling hourly summary for contractual breach detection.

Requested redlines / clarifications:
1) Aggregation window: we'd prefer the contractual measurement to use 15-minute rolling windows aggregated daily rather than hourly aggregation. This reduces the chance of long hourly anomalies masking customer-visible degradation.
2) Burst carveout: remove or severely limit the one 3-minute-per-24h automatic carveout. Greenline is not comfortable with unconstrained carveouts; acceptable alternative: allow carveout only for scheduled, communicated capacity ramps or critical production incidents declared by Greenline.
3) Definition of "successful request": please clarify whether requests returning model-level partial outputs (e.g., truncated responses due to safety filters) count as successful for latency SLOs. We expect definition to include any 2xx response where the API returned a usable payload.
4) Credits: please provide the formal credit schedule and an explicit example calculation showing how repeated hourly breaches would compound.

We are happy to compromise on hourly vs 15-minute by accepting hourly for contract if Redwood provides a specific carveout policy that is narrower than what was proposed.

Please respond with an updated operative proposal including the formal credits table and exact wording for carveouts.

Regards,
Greenline Analytics Legal
legal@greenline.ai

(Forwarded previous message from Karthik included above)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@greenline.ai>, Greenline Analytics Legal <legal@greenline.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed operational SLOs and measurement details — draft response and next steps

Ari / Greenline Legal — thanks for the quick review and helpful feedback. Appreciate the specificity on windows and carveouts — that makes negotiations faster.

Proposed compromise from Redwood:
- Aggregation windows: we will publish fine-grained customer-facing metrics at 1-minute granularity in Console and provide 15-minute rolling visibility upon request, but the contractual breach detection window will be a 1-hour aggregation. Contract language will explicitly state that Canary/Orchestrated rollout carveouts are limited to declared deployment windows and that Redwood will provide 30 minutes advance notice where operationally possible.
- Burst carveout: we will tighten this — instead of an automatic daily 3-minute carveout, Redwood will allow a single 3-minute burst carveout per 24-hour period only if it is associated with a scheduled, pre-notified capacity ramp or model swap. For emergency incidents we will not apply the carveout unless Greenline declares the incident and agrees to the carveout retrospectively.
- Successful request definition: agree to use 2xx HTTP responses with a full payload as "successful"; partial/truncated outputs caused by server-side safety filters will be considered failed for latency SLO purposes and counted against availability/error metrics.
- Credits: Karthik will produce a formal credit schedule (tabular) and an example calculation tomorrow morning and we'll include it in the contract addendum.

Next steps:
1) Karthik to draft the credits table and final operational bullets (by EOD Jan 16).
2) Redwood legal and Greenline legal to exchange tracked redlines (target contract draft by Jan 22).
3) If agreed, we will include a one-page runbook describing rollout notifications, KV-cache priming behavior, and the single-burst carveout policy.

I am attaching an initial draft (slo_commitment_draft_v1.pdf) for legal markup. If this looks broadly acceptable please confirm and we will move the redlines into a formal addendum.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
